content.text: FATAL: I can't keep running.  Or I've detected a situation where there's a risk of data loss, so I'm shutting down.
ERROR: Server detected inconsistent state between db and persistent storage, an unexpected IO error accessing either the DB or filesystem.
WARN: Sysadmin should probably know about this, or a potential cause of future error is detected.
INFO: Clearly user error, or signifant server events (startup, module initialization)
TBD: Discussion about appropriate use of INFO vs. DEBUG vs. TRACE.  General sense on the call that a lot of places where Fedora currently uses DEBUG should probably be trace.
Whoops.  I forgot that slf4j doesn't have a FATAL level....here's why:

So if we want to distinguish between application-stopping and and non-application-stopping ERRORs, we must do so within the text of the log message.  Actually saying something like "Really bad thing X happened! Shutting down Fedora..." would be fine I think.
Found the problem, you cannot change pid namespace in fedora.fcfg to whatever, this was the problem.
I still have to find a way to change the namespace.
Fedora will often report ERROR for simple operations that can hardly be called an error.
As fedora is a server system, there are really two kinds of ERRORS

For a maintenance perspective, I want my maintenance department to monitor the fedora log for problems with the fedora server. These should not monitor the logs for users timing out or not knowing the correct password.
I feel we should rework the log statements, or provide a way for the user-request problems to be filtered to a separate file.
Examples of how fedora logs errors
I pressed "next" after the session timed out. Do the server operator need to informed of this server error?
ERROR 2011-01-20 13:10:24.055 [http-7880-4] ([FieldSearchServlet]) Servlet.service() for servlet FieldSearchServlet threw exception
org.fcrepo.server.errors.UnknownSessionTokenException: Session is expired or never existed.
A user failed to login. Is this really an ERROR?
ERROR 2011-01-24 10:48:53.016 [http-7880-11] (AuthFilterJAAS) Login Failure: all modules ignored
WARN, not ERROR, but attempted to load an object that does not exist.
WARN 2011-01-24 10:53:33.513 [http-7880-3] (FedoraObjectResource) Resource not found: demo:5; unable to fulfill REST API request
Malformed pid, that is clearly a Server ERROR.
ERROR 2011-01-24 10:53:49.862 [http-7880-11] (FedoraObjectResource) Unexpected error fulfilling REST API request
Uh, getting an non-existant datastream. Is this really an ERROR?

org.fcrepo.server.errors.DatastreamNotFoundException: [DefaulAccess] No datastream could be returned. Either there is no datastream for the digital object "fedora-system:FedoraObject-3.0" with datastream ID of "VIEW "  OR  there are no datastreams that match the specified date/time value of "null "  .

fields.summary: Fedora misuse ERROR statements for logging

comments.body:
Discussion today about levels:

FATAL: I can't keep running. Or I've detected a situation where there's a risk of data loss, so I'm shutting down.
ERROR: Server detected inconsistent state between db and persistent storage, an unexpected IO error accessing either the DB or filesystem.
WARN: Sysadmin should probably know about this, or a potential cause of future error is detected.
INFO: Clearly user error, or signifant server events (startup, module initialization)
TBD: Discussion about appropriate use of INFO vs. DEBUG vs. TRACE. General sense on the call that a lot of places where Fedora currently uses DEBUG should probably be trace.

Whoops. I forgot that slf4j doesn't have a FATAL level....here's why:

http://www.slf4j.org/faq.html#fatal

So if we want to distinguish between application-stopping and and non-application-stopping ERRORs, we must do so within the text of the log message. Actually saying something like "Really bad thing X happened! Shutting down Fedora..." would be fine I think.

Exhibit 3 and 4

Found the problem, you cannot change pid namespace in fedora.fcfg to whatever, this was the problem.
I still have to find a way to change the namespace.

renderedFields.description:
Fedora will often report ERROR for simple operations that can hardly be called an error.

As fedora is a server system, there are really two kinds of ERRORS

1. User request failed
2. Server got broken

For a maintenance perspective, I want my maintenance department to monitor the fedora log for problems with the fedora server. These should not monitor the logs for users timing out or not knowing the correct password.

I feel we should rework the log statements, or provide a way for the user-request problems to be filtered to a separate file.

Examples of how fedora logs errors
